name: Video
tip: short videos: narrated shorts, lists, stories, explainers, ads and cinematic clips
about: Short videos from one sentence. A narrated short: a script built to keep the title's promise (a hook, a structure, a tone, an ending ask), a picture per cut, a voice, word-by-word captions in the platforms' safe zone, a slow camera move, transitions and music - cut together by Cutroom. A cinematic clip: one key picture brought to life - by Wan on the graphics card, or by a camera move where there is none - with music under it. Each comes with the post text for its platforms.

settings.label: Kind of video
settings.tip: By the job: a topic, a story, an explainer or an ad with something to say becomes a narrated short (script, a picture per scene, voice, subtitles); one moment, mood or shot with no voice becomes a cinematic clip

about.Narrated short: a video with something to say - a topic, list, story, explainer or ad - narrated over a picture per scene, with captions
about.Cinematic clip: one moment, mood or shot brought to life, with no voice

settings.label: Structure
settings.tip: How the narration is built. By the job: what fits the topic - a title that promises a number (three things, five tips) is a numbered list that delivers exactly that many, each named and explained

settings.label: Tone
settings.tip: How it sounds: informative, funny, dramatic, inspiring or persuasive; by the job: what fits the topic

settings.label: Hook
settings.tip: The first line, made to stop the scroll: a question, a bold claim, a surprising fact or the start of a story

settings.label: Length (s)
settings.tip: a narrated short: its narration is written to this length; a cinematic clip is 5 s of motion per shot

settings.label: Ending ask
settings.tip: Said at the end, word for word ("Follow for part two") - empty: the narration ends on its own last idea

settings.label: Language
settings.tip: The language the narration, captions and post text are written in

settings.label: Shape
settings.tip: 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts; 16:9 for YouTube; 1:1 for a feed post

settings.label: Look
settings.tip: the art style of every picture in the video

settings.label: Picture motion
settings.tip: Narrated short: a slow camera move on every picture keeps the frame alive, or the pictures held still

settings.label: Framing
settings.tip: Fill: each picture cropped to fill the frame; Fit: the whole picture, with bars where it does not fill it

settings.label: Voice
settings.tip: The narrator (edge-tts voices, free)

settings.label: Voice speed
settings.tip: 1.0 is the voice's own pace; shorts read best a little quicker

settings.label: Captions
settings.tip: Words on the picture as they are spoken - most short videos are watched with the sound off

settings.label: Caption style
settings.tip: Word pop: each word appears with a small bounce as it is said; Word by word: the same without the bounce; Sentence: a line at a time

settings.label: Caption place
settings.tip: Lower third keeps the words clear of the platforms' buttons and captions at the bottom of a vertical feed

settings.label: Caption size
settings.tip: Text height in pixels on a 1080-wide frame

settings.label: Caption colour
settings.tip: The colour of the words

settings.label: Outline
settings.tip: A dark edge around each letter so it reads on any picture; 0: none

settings.label: Box behind words
settings.tip: A dark rounded box behind the words

settings.label: Font
settings.tip: Bold and Clean: Be Vietnam Pro; Display: Kabel; Script: Charm

settings.label: Cut every (s)
settings.tip: The longest a picture stays on screen; the script plans one picture for each

settings.label: Transition
settings.tip: How one picture gives way to the next: a hard cut, a fade, a slide, a zoom, or a mix

settings.label: Music
settings.tip: Music under the voice

settings.label: Music level
settings.tip: How loud the music sits under the voice (0.1-0.2 keeps every word clear)

settings.label: How a clip moves
settings.tip: By the job: Wan animates the key picture on a machine with a graphics card; on a machine without one, or when Wan does not pass or runs far past its usual time, a slow camera move over the picture

settings.label: Frame size
settings.tip: By the job: from the shape

settings.label: Wan clip width
settings.tip: By the job: from the shape, at the size Wan 2.2 draws well on an 8 GB card

settings.label: Wan clip height
settings.tip: By the job: from the shape

subject: what the video is about in one sentence of at most 24 words: the topic, product or story and who it is for - no camera words, no style words

recipe.title: Script and scenes
recipe.does: the script of the short: a hook in the first line, one idea per sentence, an ending that lands - and one picture per scene

args.brief: You are the writer and director of a short video. Write its narration and its scenes, in {language}. The narration is spoken aloud over about {seconds} seconds: about 2.3 words a second, so close to that many words. Structure: {structure} - By the job means the one that fits the topic best; whatever the structure, the video keeps the promise of its topic: a topic that names a number (three things, five tips) is a numbered list of exactly that many points, each named in plain words and explained in a sentence or two, never fewer, never merged. Tone: {tone}. The first sentence is the hook ({hook}; By the job: the strongest for this topic) - it makes a viewer stay in under two seconds, with no greeting and no 'in this video'. One idea per sentence, plain spoken words, an ending that lands - then, when it is not empty, this ending ask word for word: "{call_to_action}". No 'in conclusion', no hashtags, no emoji, no stage directions. The scenes are the pictures shown while it is spoken, in order: one for about every {cut_seconds} seconds (at least 3, at most 14), each showing what is being said at that moment. Each scene's prompt is for a picture model that reads only the start of a prompt and remembers nothing between pictures: at most 40 words, the subject first, then what it does, the setting, the light, the camera; vary the shots (close-up, wide, over the shoulder, detail) so no two scenes look alike; a recurring character is described again in every prompt with the same few words (build, hair, clothes, colours). No writing, logos or text in any picture.

shape.title: the video's title, at most 8 words
shape.narration: the whole narration as one paragraph

recipe.title: A picture for every scene
recipe.does: each scene drawn in the video's look and shape

recipe.title: Voice, captions, music and the cut (Cutroom)
recipe.does: Cutroom speaks the narration, times word-by-word captions to the voice, moves the camera over each picture and cuts the scenes in order, with music under the voice

recipe.title: The shot
recipe.does: one shot, written like a director of photography: the key picture, how it moves, the music under it

args.brief: You are a director of photography planning ONE cinematic shot of about 5 seconds. Write the key picture (for a picture model that reads only the start of a prompt: at most 45 words, the subject first, then its action frozen at its best moment, the setting, the light with its direction and colour, the lens and angle; no writing in the picture), how the shot moves (one sentence for a video model: what the subject does, ONE camera move - slow push-in, orbit left, crane up, handheld follow - and how the light behaves; calm motion keeps the picture's design) and the music under it (genre, instruments, mood, tempo as words).
